name: r6-m01
statement: The cued base's deliberative register is held only by attention back to the 3-token cue at the start of the answer, so it fades with distance from the cue: past about 8,000 tokens the cued base writes fewer first-person deliberation words and slides into pretraining-style textbook continuation (new 'Problem/Exercise/Solution:' blocks and restarted derivations), and its long hard328 answers are lost to this register decay, not to loops or to failing to stop, whereas RL has the register in its weights and keeps it at every length.
scope: Covers Olmo-3-1025-7B base with the opening cue against Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (plain), at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, on hard328 and on the long tail of MATH-500 (answers over about 8,000 tokens). Does not cover the T 0.6 loops (a different failure, rule-A loops; knowledge-787e53), short wrong base answers (slips, misreads; result-afc423), the Code pair, or vote and restart rules. It says nothing about weight-delta scale. Conflicts found and listed: result-882fa7, result-a6ab7a, result-855858.

imports.finding: Alignment changes few token decisions, concentrated in stylistic tokens at the start of a response, and the base-vs-aligned KL falls with position.
imports.how: The cue is such a start-of-response style shift injected only by prefill. Its effect on later tokens has to be carried by attention to those first positions, so it is expected to weaken as the answer grows. RL instead changes the weights, so its effect is present at every position.

explains.quote: 140 base first answers exceed 12,000 tokens (11 right)
explains.how: Past 12,000 tokens the register has decayed and the base is no longer solving the problem, so almost none of these answers are right.

explains.quote: its cap hits on the 328 are failures to solve, not failures to stop
explains.how: Once the register is gone the text has left problem-solving behind, so forcing a commit late in it extracts guesses.

explains.quote: At T 1.0 rule A finds 0 loops in T1, T2 and T3
explains.how: Register decay yields fresh, incompressible textbook-style text rather than repeated blocks, so the long failures carry no loop signature.

explains.quote: from the RL model's prefix it finishes far more often
explains.how: An RL prefix is dense in register close to the generation point, which partly replaces the far-away cue that the decaying attention can no longer reach.
The gap grows with answer length because decay grows with distance from the cue, while RL's register does not decay.

explains.quote: the first 100 RL steps install the opening the cue forces
explains.how: RL writes the register into the weights early, which is the non-decaying copy of what the cue supplies only through context.

explains.quote: with top-8, Wait/perhaps/Hmm rates rise to RL's level
explains.how: Weight directions that carry the deliberation register keep it in long answers, and with them cap hits fall from 77 to 46.

explains.quote: Late-MLP top directions x base lm_head read as deliberation words
explains.how: The RL delta's main directions write the deliberation register directly into the weights.

explains.quote: the model invents and answers a new problem after its real answer
explains.how: Without a held register the base falls back to pretraining-style continuation that starts new problems, the textbook mode this theory predicts for long answers.

conflicts.quote: giving the cued base the RL model's Wait habit does not raise MATH-500
conflicts.how: A register push held for the whole answer should help if decay costs accuracy. The reply that MATH-500 has few answers past 8,000 tokens limits this conflict, but does not remove it.

conflicts.quote: Base fails RL prefixes mostly by cap hit
conflicts.how: Even from a register-dense RL prefix the base often runs to the cap. The theory can account for this only if the register decays again with distance from the prefix, which it does not state in advance.

conflicts.quote: markers do not separate right from wrong samples of the same model
conflicts.how: If register loss drives failure, whole-answer marker density should be lower in wrong (longer) base samples, and it is barely lower. The theory places the loss in the late part of long answers only, which a whole-answer average dilutes.

rival: Failure-drift (difficulty) rival: long base answers are on problems the base cannot solve. After exhausting its approaches it gives up, and any loss of deliberation is a consequence of failing, not of distance from the cue. The two separate on long base answers that end right. Distance-driven decay predicts that these answers also lose register late (median late/early marker ratio well under 1). Failure-drift predicts that they keep RL's level (about 1.0). A second test: re-inserting the cue partway through a long answer restores register and rescues problems under this theory, but does nothing beyond a fresh continuation under the rival.

predictions.experiment: Late-vs-early deliberation density on long answers, base minus RL: the median over rows of r = (M_late + 1) / (M_early + 1), cued base minus RL, on hard328 answers of at least 12,000 tokens.
predictions.recipe: Files: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and the same path for abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef (RL plain), fetched from s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/<job-id>/answers.jsonl as in inventory.md. In each file keep one row per problem_index (the first in file order), then keep rows with n_generated >= 12000. Cap hits are included. Let t = the text field and L = len(t). Decile k (k = 1..10) = t[floor((k-1)*L/10) : floor(k*L/10)]. In each decile separately count non-overlapping matches (Python re.findall, case-sensitive) of (?<![A-Za-z])(Let me|I'm|I'll|Okay|Wait|Hmm|I|me)(?![A-Za-z]). M_early = count in decile 2 + count in decile 3. M_late = count in decile 8 + count in decile 9. Per row r = (M_late + 1) / (M_early + 1). Per file take the median of r over the kept rows (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values). Statistic = median(e72c) - median(86ef). If either file has fewer than 5 kept rows, the prediction counts as refuted.

predictions.experiment: Late onset of textbook blocks in long cued-base answers: the share of hard328 base answers of at least 12,000 tokens that contain a textbook header line in their second half and none in their first half.
predictions.recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue, hard328, T 1.0). Keep one row per problem_index (the first in file order), then keep rows with n_generated >= 12000. Cap hits are included. Let t = text and L = len(t). Split t on '\n' and record each line's start offset in t. A line is a header if re.match(r'\s*(?:(?:Problem|Exercise|Question|Example)\s*\d*\s*[:.]|Solution\s*:)', line) succeeds (case-sensitive). A row counts if it has at least one header line with start offset >= L/2 and no header line with start offset < L/2. Statistic = counted rows / kept rows.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test, register decay in long base answers that end right. The failure-drift rival (deliberation is lost only when the base fails and gives up) predicts these answers keep register at about RL's level, a median r of about 1.0 (0.95 to 1.1). Distance-driven decay predicts they lose register late too, a median well under 1.
predictions.recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue, hard328, T 1.0). Keep one row per problem_index (the first in file order), then keep rows with cap_hit false, score_v3 == 1 and n_generated > 10000. Rows with a missing or null score_v3 are dropped. Compute r = (M_late + 1) / (M_early + 1) exactly as in the first prediction: deciles of the text by character, the same regex, M_early = deciles 2+3, M_late = deciles 8+9. Statistic = median of r over the kept rows (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values). Report it whatever the number of kept rows; if no row qualifies, it counts as refuted.

predictions.experiment: Cue re-insertion on long base answers, GPU. Take the cued base's stored hard328 T 1.0 answers (job abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c) whose n_generated exceeds 8,000 (the 184 answers of result-51fd20). Cut each at 8,000 generated tokens and continue with the base model (prompt = cue prompt + the 8,000-token prefix) at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 up to the 16,384 total cap, in two arms with the same per-row seeds: (A) no inserted text; (B) the text '\n\nOkay' appended at the cut, before continuing. Grade the full prefix + continuation with v3. The statistic is right(B) minus right(A), of the 184. Both arms together are about 3 M generated tokens, about 50 minutes on one H100 at the measured ~1,050 tok/s. The failure-drift rival predicts about 0 (within +-3).
predictions.refuted_by: B minus A <= 2 problems, or arm B's continuation has a marker density (regex of the first prediction, per 1,000 characters of continuation) no higher than arm A's
